info.title: Community API
info.summary: A community for your app: topics, posts, comments, reactions and notifications.
info.description:
The community API gives an app a members' community: topics, a feed of posts
with images, comments and replies, emoji reactions, search, blocking, reports,
notifications and live updates. Each customer (a creator) has one community,
kept apart from every other customer's.

## Keys and users

Every request carries an API key in `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

- A **secret key** belongs on the customer's backend only. It can do
  everything, and names the end user it acts for in `X-External-Id`.
- A **publishable key** ships in the app. It reaches one user's data only
  together with a **session token** in `X-Community-Session`.

A session token comes from `POST /v1/auth/session`. The app mints its own
with the publishable key (the device SDKs do this in `initialize(userId)`),
or the customer's backend mints one with the secret key.

Each operation says who may call it in `x-community-auth`: `any_key`,
`member` (one end user), `creator` (secret key only), `member_or_creator`,
or `session`.

## Conventions

- Ids shown to clients are public ids such as `cm_post_…`. Users are named by
  the customer's own id for them, the external id.
- Times are RFC 3339 in UTC.
- Lists are read a page at a time with opaque cursors. A cursor is null when
  there is nothing to fetch with it.
- A partial edit (`PATCH`) changes only the fields that are sent.
- Deletes, pins, reactions, blocks and "mark read" are safe to repeat.
- Image links are short-lived. Read them again rather than storing them.

## Errors

Every non-2xx reply has the same body, `ErrorEnvelope`, with a `code` from a
closed list. Branch on `code`, never on `message`. `fields` names the fields
that failed, for `validation_failed`. `x-community-codes` on each error
response lists the codes that route can answer with.

get.description:
Says which customer and environment the key belongs to. The quickest way to check that a key works.

**Who may call it.** Any key: secret or publishable.

post.summary: Mint a session for one end user
post.description:
Returns a session token for the named user. With a secret key, your backend mints it after authenticating the user itself. With a publishable key, the app mints its own: this is what the device SDKs do in `initialize(userId)`. A session works for that one user only and lasts at most 24 hours. With a publishable key the app names its own user, so the session does not prove who they are.

**Who may call it.** Any key: secret or publishable.

201.description: The new session. The token is shown once.

delete.description:
Ends the session whose token is sent. The token stops working at once.

**Who may call it.** A publishable key with the session token to end.

get.summary: The user a call acts for
get.description:
Echoes the end user named by the session token or by `X-External-Id`.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

delete.description:
Removes the user and everything stored for them: profile, posts, comments, reactions, images, blocks, reports and notifications. Erasing an unknown user is not an error.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only: the creator's backend.

get.summary: Own profile and whether the user has joined
get.description:
Not having joined is a normal answer (`joined` false, `profile` null), not an error. It is the app's cue to show the Welcome screen.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

200.description: Whether the user has joined, and their profile.

patch.description:
Changes the user's own username, bio, photo or background. Send only the fields to change. A photo or background is an image uploaded through `POST /v1/media`.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

get.description:
A hint for the form while the user types. A taken or badly formed name is a normal answer, not an error. Joining decides in the end.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The name to check.

post.summary: Join the community under a username
post.description:
Makes the user a member. Joining again under the same name returns the profile unchanged (200), so a retry is safe.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

200.description: This user had already joined under this name.

201.description: Joined. The body is the new profile.

get.description:
How many members the community has, and the profile photos of up to four members who have one, picked at random on every call. For the card that leads into the community. The user need not have joined. A member is never shown someone they have a block with; the count is the whole community either way.

**Who may call it.** For one end user (a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`), or the creator's backend with a secret key alone.

Read only: a profile is edited only by its owner. The creator can turn viewing other profiles off; a member can always open their own.

**Who may call it.** For one end user (a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`), or the creator's backend with a secret key alone, which also sees hidden topics.

patch.description:
Sets the member's role. Setting the role they already hold changes nothing.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only: the creator's backend.

200.description: The member's profile with the new role.

get.description:
Everyone who has joined, in username order, each with their role. For the creator's dashboard.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only: the creator's backend.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only members whose username contains this text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Only members with this role.

get.description:
Members see live topics only. The creator's backend also sees hidden ones.

**Who may call it.** For one end user (a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`), or the creator's backend with a secret key alone, which also sees hidden topics.

parameters.name: trending
parameters.description: `true` returns only trending topics.

post.description:
Adds a topic to the community.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only: the creator's backend.

get.description:
A hidden topic is not found for a member.

**Who may call it.** For one end user (a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`), or the creator's backend with a secret key alone, which also sees hidden topics.

patch.description:
Send only the fields to change.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only: the creator's backend.

delete.description:
Removes the topic and its posts. Deleting one that is already gone is not an error.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only: the creator's backend.

get.description:
Posts newest first, for one topic or for all. Pinned posts come in `pinned` on the first page. Posts across a block, and posts in hidden topics, are left out. Send `before` or `after`, not both.

**Who may call it.** For one end user (a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`), or the creator's backend with a secret key alone, which also sees hidden topics.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: A `next_cursor`: the next older posts.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: A `prev_cursor` (the page before, pages mode) or a `newest_cursor` (posts created since).

post.description:
Text, images, or both, in a live topic. The user must have joined the community.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

200.description: This `Idempotency-Key` was already used by this user: the first post.

201.description: Posted. The body is the new post.

get.description:
Not found when the post is gone, hidden, or across a block.

**Who may call it.** For one end user (a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`), or the creator's backend with a secret key alone, which also sees hidden topics.

delete.description:
A member deletes their own posts; the creator's backend deletes any. The post, its comments, reactions and images are removed for good. Deleting one that is already gone is not an error.

**Who may call it.** For one end user (a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`), or the creator's backend with a secret key alone, which also sees hidden topics.

put.description:
Keeps the post on top of the feed. Any post can be pinned, however old, with no limit on how many. Safe to repeat.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only: the creator's backend.

delete.description:
Puts the post back in its normal place by date. Safe to repeat.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only: the creator's backend.

get.description:
A post matches when its text contains every word, in any order and case. The last word may be only the start of a word. No match is an empty list.

**Who may call it.** For one end user (a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`), or the creator's backend with a secret key alone, which also sees hidden topics.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The words to find, at least 2 characters.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: A `next_cursor`: the next page of older matches.

put.description:
Gives the emoji. A user can give several different emoji but not the same one twice; sending it again changes nothing. The reply is the post's full reaction list.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

delete.summary: Take a reaction back from a post
delete.description:
Removes the user's emoji. Removing one that is not there changes nothing.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

put.description:
The same rules as reacting to a post.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

delete.summary: Take a reaction back from a comment
delete.description:
Removes the user's emoji. Removing one that is not there changes nothing.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

get.description:
Top-level comments, oldest first. Replies are read per comment.

**Who may call it.** For one end user (a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`), or the creator's backend with a secret key alone, which also sees hidden topics.

post.summary: Comment on a post, or reply to a comment
post.description:
Text, images, or both. `parent_id` makes it a reply, when the creator has turned replies on.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

200.description: This `Idempotency-Key` was already used by this user: the first comment.

201.description: Added. The body is the new comment.

get.description:
Replies to one comment, oldest first.

**Who may call it.** For one end user (a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`), or the creator's backend with a secret key alone, which also sees hidden topics.

delete.description:
A member deletes their own comments; the creator's backend deletes any. Deleting one that is already gone is not an error.

**Who may call it.** For one end user (a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`), or the creator's backend with a secret key alone, which also sees hidden topics.

post.description:
Step 1 of 3. Returns a link to send the file to. Send the file's bytes to `upload.url` with `upload.method`, then finish the upload.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

Step 3 of 3. The server checks the file and stores it as JPEG in two sizes: longest side 1024 pixels and 512 pixels. The image can then be put on a post, a comment or a profile.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

get.description:
The user's own upload.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

get.summary: The member's coaching chat at a glance
get.description:
How many of the coach's messages the member has not seen, and when the last message was sent. Every member has one chat with their coach; it is made by its first message, and before that this answers zero and null. Whether the member's subscription lets them use the chat is the app's decision and is not checked here.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

200.description: The unread count and the last message time.

get.summary: One page of the coaching chat
get.description:
Messages oldest first, as the screen shows them. With no cursor, the newest messages. `before` gives the ones above (scrolling up); `after` gives the ones below, which is also how to catch up after a live event or a dropped connection; `around` gives the page with that message in the middle, for jumping to a search result. Send at most one of the three. A member with no chat yet gets an empty page.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 100. Left out, 30.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: An `older_cursor`: the messages before that page.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: A `newer_cursor`: the messages after that page.

parameters.name: around
parameters.description: A message id: the page with that message in the middle.

post.summary: Send a message to the coach
post.description:
Text, images, or both. Images are uploaded first with `POST /v1/media`. Sending also marks the chat read for the member.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

200.description: This `Idempotency-Key` was already used by this user: the first message.

201.description: Sent. The body is the new message.

patch.description:
Changes the text of one of the member's own messages and sets `edited_at`. Its images stay. The text may be emptied only when the message has images. Sending the text it already has changes nothing.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

200.description: The message as it is now.

delete.description:
Deletes one of the member's own messages for good, with its images. Deleting one that is already gone is not an error. The coach's message cannot be deleted by the member.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

post.description:
Records that the member has seen everything in the chat so far. Send it when the chat is open and a message from the coach is on screen. Sending it again changes nothing more.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

200.description: The unread count, now zero, and the last message time.

get.description:
The messages of the member's chat whose text contains every word of `q`; the last word may be only the start of one. Newest first. No match is an empty list. To show a result in place, read the chat with `around` set to its id.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The words to look for, at least 2 characters.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 100. Left out, 30.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: A `next_cursor` from the page before: the next older matches.

post.summary: Start the upload of a voice note or a document
post.description:
The coach's side of the chat can send a voice note or a document. This records the file and returns a link to send its bytes to. Send them with the method given, then call the complete route, then name the file in `file_ids` when sending a message. A voice note may be any audio type. A document must be a PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, RTF, text or CSV file. A file that is never put on a message is removed after a day.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only, with `X-External-Id` naming a member whose role is `coach` or `creator`: the creator's backend, acting as that coach.

post.summary: Finish the upload of a voice note or a document
post.description:
Says the file has been sent to its link. The server checks it arrived and is within the limit, and marks it ready to put on a message. Safe to repeat. A file that is empty or over the limit is refused and removed: start a new upload.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only, with `X-External-Id` naming a member whose role is `coach` or `creator`: the creator's backend, acting as that coach.

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description: The file's id, from starting the upload.

200.description: Ready. The body is the file.

get.description:
Every member's chat that has a message in it, the one with the newest message first: the coach's inbox. Each row has the member, how many of their messages the coach's side has not seen, and the newest message for a preview line. Every coach and the creator see the same list; a chat is with the coach's side, not with one person. `next_cursor`, sent as `before`, gives the next page.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only, with `X-External-Id` naming a member whose role is `coach` or `creator`: the creator's backend, acting as that coach.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 100. Left out, 30.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: A `next_cursor`: the chats after that page.

parameters.name: unread
parameters.description: `true` for only the chats with something the coach's side has not seen.

get.summary: One page of a member's chat, as the coach
get.description:
One member's chat as the coach's side sees it, oldest first, with the same `before`, `after` and `around` as the member's own read. `is_mine` is true on the messages the coach's side wrote, and `is_read` on them says the member has seen them. Reading does not mark the chat read; send `POST /v1/coach-chat/members/{external_id}/read` for that. A member with no chat yet gives an empty page.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only, with `X-External-Id` naming a member whose role is `coach` or `creator`: the creator's backend, acting as that coach.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 100. Left out, 30.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: An `older_cursor`: the messages before that page.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: A `newer_cursor`: the messages after that page.

parameters.name: around
parameters.description: A message id: the page with that message in the middle.

post.summary: Send a message to a member, as the coach
post.description:
Adds a message from the coach's side to one member's chat, making the chat if this is its first message. Text, images, files, or any mix. Images are uploaded first with `POST /v1/media`, files with `POST /v1/coach-chat/files`, both as the same coach. Sending also marks the chat read for the coach's side, so the member's own messages show as read.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only, with `X-External-Id` naming a member whose role is `coach` or `creator`: the creator's backend, acting as that coach.

200.description: This `Idempotency-Key` was already used by this sender in this chat: the first message.

201.description: Sent. The body is the new message, as its sender sees it.

post.summary: Mark a member's chat read, as the coach
post.description:
Records that the coach's side has seen everything in the member's chat so far, so the member's own messages show as read in their app. Send it when the coach has the chat open. Sending it again changes nothing more.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only, with `X-External-Id` naming a member whose role is `coach` or `creator`: the creator's backend, acting as that coach.

200.description: The chat for the coach's side: `unread_count` is the member's messages not yet seen, now zero.

put.summary: Register a phone for push notifications
put.description:
Stores the phone's push token for the user. The token is an Expo push token or a Firebase Cloud Messaging token; the kind is worked out from its form unless `provider` says. Registering the same token again changes nothing. A token registered by another user of the same community moves to this one.

From then on each notification is also sent to the phone, with `data` for opening the right screen: `type` (`community.notification`), `notification_id`, `kind`, `post_id` and, when there is a comment, `comment_id` and `parent_comment_id`. A message from the member's coach is a notification too, of kind `coach_message`; its `data` has `type` (`community.coach_message`), `notification_id`, `kind` and `message_id`: open the coaching chat. Its title is the coach's username and its text is the message, or what was sent when it has no text.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

post.description:
Removes the user's push token: send it when the user signs out. Removing a token that is not registered is not an error.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

get.description:
Whether the user wants push notifications, whether the creator allows them, and how many phones are registered. Push arrives only when both switches are on.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

put.summary: Turn the user's push notifications on or off
put.description:
Off stops messages to the user's phones; notifications still appear in the list. Something missed while off is not sent later.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

200.description: The switch as it is now.

get.description:
The members this user has blocked.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

put.description:
After a block neither sees the other's posts, comments, profile, notifications or live events. Blocking again changes nothing.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

delete.description:
Removing a block that is not there is not an error.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

post.description:
One member can report one post once. When the number of different reporters reaches the creator's `report_threshold`, the post is removed from the community: members no longer see it. It is kept in the moderation archive, not deleted.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

200.description: This member had already reported it.

post.description:
The same rules as reporting a post.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

200.description: This member had already reported it.

get.description:
Reports on the community's posts and comments, for the creator's dashboard.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only: the creator's backend.

Posts and comments that reached the report threshold. They are not deleted: members no longer see them, and they are kept here with their whole text, pictures, author and the members who reported them. Newest first.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only: the creator's backend.

One item of the moderation archive, by its archive id.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only: the creator's backend.

Newest first. Notifications across a block, or about hidden topics, are left out. A message from the member's coach is in the list too, as kind `coach_message`, with `message_id` instead of a post. There is one such row for the chat, not one per message: a new message replaces it, with the newest message and a new `id`. Reading the coaching chat marks it read.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

How many notifications are unread.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

post.description:
Marks everything the user has now as read. Sending it again changes nothing more.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

Sent when the user opens a notification. Safe to repeat.

**Who may call it.** For one end user: a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`.

get.description:
Any key can read them, so the app can adapt to them.

**Who may call it.** Any key: secret or publishable.

patch.description:
Send only the fields to change. Lowering `report_threshold` removes at once whatever already has that many reports, and the reply says how much.

**Who may call it.** Secret key only: the creator's backend.

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket that receives one JSON object per change, each a `LiveEvent`. The first message is `{"type":"ready"}`. The connection only listens: posting, reacting and commenting use their own routes. Send `{"type":"watch","topic_id":"…"}` to follow one topic, or an empty `topic_id` for all. Events from another community, from hidden topics and across a block are never delivered. A user may hold at most 5 connections.

**Who may call it.** For one end user (a publishable key with a session token, or a secret key with `X-External-Id`), or the creator's backend with a secret key alone, which also sees hidden topics.

parameters.name: topic_id
parameters.description: Follow only this topic from the start.

apiKey.description: A secret key (`cm_sk_…`, backend only) or a publishable key (`cm_pk_…`, in the app).

SessionHeader.name: X-Community-Session
SessionHeader.description: The session token, with a publishable key. Names the end user the call acts for.

ExternalIdHeader.name: X-External-Id
ExternalIdHeader.description: Your own id for the end user, with a secret key. Names the end user the call acts for.

MediaId.name: media_id
MediaId.description: The image's id, from starting the upload.

ExternalId.name: external_id
ExternalId.description: Your own id for the user.

Emoji.name: emoji
Emoji.description: The emoji, percent-encoded. Any emoji; skin tones count as separate emoji.

LimitPosts.name: limit
LimitPosts.description: Page size, 1 to 40: the app's choice. Left out, 20.

LimitSearch.name: limit
LimitSearch.description: Page size, 1 to 40. Left out, the creator's `search_page_size`.

Before.name: before
Before.description: A `next_cursor` from the page before: the next older items.

After.name: after
After.description: A `next_cursor` from the page before: the next items.

TopicFilter.name: topic_id
TopicFilter.description: Only this topic's posts. Left out, every topic.

Idempotency.name: Idempotency-Key
Idempotency.description: A key you choose, 1 to 255 printable characters. A request retried with the same key by the same user writes nothing and returns the first result.

Session.description: A session token for one end user. The token appears in this reply and nowhere else.

token.description: The session token. Send it in the header named by `header`.

token_type.description: Always `opaque`: the token carries nothing to decode.

header.description: The request header the token is sent in.

external_id.description: The user the session is for.

environment.description: `test` or `live`, the environment of the key that minted it.

SessionRequest.description: Who the session is for and how long it lasts.

external_id.description: Your own id for the end user, 1 to 255 printable characters.

ttl_seconds.description: Lifetime in seconds, 60 to 86400. Left out, one hour.

WhoAmI.description: Which customer and key the service sees.

key_id.description: The key's public id (not the key itself).

EndUser.description: The end user a call acts for.

external_id.description: Your own id for the user.

via_session.description: True when the user was named by a session token, false when by `X-External-Id`.

ErasedUser.description: The result of erasing an end user.

deleted.description: False when there was nobody by that id, which is not an error.

external_id.description: Your own id for the user.

username.description: The name the member chose in the community.

avatar_url.description: A short-lived link to their photo, or an empty string.

role.description: The label shown beside their name.

Image.description: One picture on a post or comment. Every image is stored in two sizes: a large one for a post opened on its own screen, and a small one for the feed.

url.description: A short-lived link to the large size: longest side at most 1024 pixels.

width.description: Width of the large size, in pixels.

height.description: Height of the large size, in pixels.

small_url.description: A short-lived link to the small size: longest side at most 512 pixels. For an image uploaded before two sizes were stored, or one already 512 pixels or less, this is the same picture as `url`.

small_height.description: Height of the small size, in pixels.

Reaction.description: One emoji on a post or comment.

body.description: The text. May be empty when the post has images.

reactions.description: The emoji on the post, in the creator's chosen order.

comments_count.description: How many comments and replies the post has.

pinned_at.description: When it was pinned, or null.

pinned.description: Pinned posts, most recently pinned first. First page only; never repeated in `posts`.

newest_cursor.description: Send as `after` later for posts created since this read.

has_more.description: True when there are more posts in the direction that was read.

page_size.description: How many posts this read was limited to: the `limit` sent, or 20.

has_more.description: True when there is another page.
